sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THROUGH PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 22.10.2019 passed by the Senior Civil Judge & MACT,
Channagiri (for short 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.934/2017, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 10.08.2017 at about 3.00 p.m. the petitioner was driving his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA.17/EK-0916 near Channagiri, at that time, a car bearing registration No.KA.50/M-8943 being driven in a rash and negligent manner and duly insured with the second respondent, came and dashed the motor cycle, because of which, the petitioner sustained the following injuries:-
1. Blunt injury over the right ankle 2.
Deep contusion 8x5 c.m. right leg 3.
3 to 5 abrasions 5x2 c.m. over the left leg 4.
3 to 4 abrasions 3x2 c.m. over the left arm
5. Blunt injury head & back 6.
Grazed abrasions 20x15 c.m. over the back 4.

The Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,22,600/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum under the following heads:-
1 Pain and suffering Rs. 25,000-00 2 Loss of amenities Rs. 15,000-00 3 Loss of future earning Rs. 93,600-00 4 Nursing and attendance Rs. 3,000-00 Medical &

2 other incidental 5

Rs . 80,000-00 charges 6 Loss of earning during treatment Rs.
6,000-00 Total Rs.2,22,600-00
5. Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
6. The only point that arise for consideration is:-
Whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal requires to be enhanced?
7. The accident happened in the year 2017.
The petitioner was aged 48 years.
His income has not been established before the Tribunal.
He has suffered 10% disability to the total body.
Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok-Adalath chart has to be considered which will be Rs.11,000/- per month.

Given his age, the multiplier of '13' has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.&
Anr reported in 2009(6) SCC 121.

sentences.text: Thus, towards 'loss of future earning', the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,71,600/- (11000x12x13x10%) as against Rs.93,600/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Towards 'loss of income during laid up period', if we take the laid up period to be three months, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- (11,000x3=33,000), as against Rs.6,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
Towards 'pain and suffering', given the nature of injuries it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.40,000/- as against Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Towards '
loss of amenities' a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
In my opinion, it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.20,000/-.
Towards ' nursing and attendance, a sum of Rs.3,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
In my opinion, the same is appropriate and correct.

Towards 'medical and other incidental charges, based on the actual bills submitted by the petitioner, a sum of Rs.80,000/-
is awarded by the tribunal.
I deem the same to be correct.
8. Thus, the compensation to the petitioner under different heads is modified as hereunder:-

4 Nursing and attendance 3,000-00 3,000-00  Medical & other  5 80,000-00 80,000-00  incidental charges  Loss of earning during

Total 2,22,600-00 3,47,600-00 Veerappa vs Raghavendra on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155013042/
3  9.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,25,000/-(Rs.3,47,600/- - Rs.2,22,600/-).

Hence, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is partly allowed;
ii) The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,25,000/-(Rupees One Lakh Twenty Five Thousand only) over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization.
iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company shall pay the enhanced compensation to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of the judgment and order.
iv) Draw modified award accordingly.
SD/-
